title: One lien, two truths
intro: Retrieval says lien 2022-FL-0044120 is terminated. The registry says it is active. Concatenation puts both in the window and lets position decide — and $340,000 of exposure disappears from a credit memo without anyone choosing to remove it.

provenance.source: a narrated multi-source UCC risk assembly; sources, trust tiers, dates and exposure figures are plausible inventions, not measurements

foot: The step this walks is M11's Fusing Three UCC Sources — dedupe by normalized fact, resolve by trust then freshness, flag genuine conflicts, and attach provenance to every surviving line.

steps.title: Four streams, one window, arrival order
narrative: A single credit call pulls from four places at once: retrieved filing chunks, a live get_debtor_history call against the state registry, the session's memory of this debtor, and the analyst's own message. Eleven items, 2,640 tokens, assembled in whatever order the futures resolved.

The output is confident and wrong in two separate ways. It reports two active liens totalling $1,675,000, because a retrieval chunk saying 2022-FL-0044120: terminated arrived after the registry result saying the same lien is active, and later text won. And it describes the 2024 Redline lien as "confirmed by three independent sources", which is three copies of one registry record.
Nothing in the assembly decided either of those things. Position decided the first and duplication decided the second.
steps.youDo: Dump your assembled context to a file and read it as a document. Every contradiction and every repeated fact you can spot by eye is one the model is also resolving by accident.

terminal.text: total secured exposure for ACME LOGISTICS & DISTRIBUTION, L.L.C.?
ctx = retrieval_chunks + tool_result + session_memory + user_msg   # arrival order
ACME has 2 active liens totalling $1,675,000. The 2024 Redline lien is confirmed by three independent sources.
"three independent sources" = one registry record, echoed three times

steps.title: The duplicate that voted three times
narrative: Dedupe first, because it is cheap and it changes what the model believes. Normalise each item to the fact it asserts — here lien:2024-FL-0019988 — and keep exactly one copy, the best-attributed: highest trust tier, then newest.

Three items collapse to one. That is 630 tokens down to 210, which is the boring half of the win. The interesting half is that the surviving line is now one claim with one provenance tag, and the model stops describing it as corroborated.

This is false amplification and it is specific to fusion. Any single source repeated is still one source, but a window containing the same sentence three times reads exactly like a window containing three agreeing witnesses — and the model has no way to tell those apart unless you tell it.
steps.claudeSays: I saw the Redline lien asserted three times and reported it as multiply confirmed. All three trace to registry record 2024-FL-0019988, fetched once.

terminal.text: items = dedupe(items, key=lambda it: it.fact)   # keep max((trust, ts))

lien:2024-FL-0019988   3 copies -> 1
  kept   [tool      | 2026-08-28 | trust=3]
  merged [retrieval | 2026-06-14 | trust=2]
  merged [memory    | 2026-08-28 | trust=1]
One active lien held by Redline Freight Capital LLC, per registry record 2024-FL-0019988.

cells: 2 lower-trust echoes of the same record, dropped

steps.title: The contradiction that must be decided
narrative: Now the one that matters. Two sources make incompatible claims about 2022-FL-0044120, and both of them are honest. The corpus snapshot was indexed 2026-06-14 and contains a UCC-3 termination filed 2026-05-28 — so retrieval is correctly reporting what the document store holds. The live registry, queried today, shows that termination withdrawn on 2026-07-11, three weeks after the snapshot.

Resolve on trust first, freshness second: the state registry is the authoritative tier and it is also newer, so it wins on both axes. Harbor Point's $340,000 goes back into the exposure and the total becomes $2,015,000.

But do not stop at picking a winner. The loser is not noise — it is evidence that the document corpus is eleven weeks stale on this debtor, and a withdrawn termination is exactly the pattern a credit committee wants to see rather than have quietly reconciled. Fusion emits the winning value and a conflict record carrying both provenances, and routes the call to human review.
steps.youDo: Make your fuser return {context, conflicts}, not just context. If conflicts is always empty, you are not detecting disagreement, you are overwriting it.

terminal.text: out = fuse(items)   # trust tier, then freshness; conflicts surfaced

subject: 2022-FL-0044120
  [tool      | 2026-08-28 | trust=3] status=active     (termination withdrawn 2026-07-11)
  [retrieval | 2026-06-14 | trust=2] status=terminated (UCC-3 filed 2026-05-28)
winner: tool(2026-08-28, trust=3) — active — overrides retrieval(2026-06-14, trust=2)
⚠ material conflict on 2022-FL-0044120 — flagged in the memo, routed to human review

Total secured exposure $2,015,000 across 3 active liens. One conflict: the document corpus shows 2022-FL-0044120 terminated as of 2026-06-14; the registry shows that termination withdrawn 2026-07-11. Registry value used.

after.title: AFTER — resolved by trust, then freshness, and flagged

conflicts.subject: 2022-FL-0044120
conflicts.why: higher trust tier and newer; termination of 2026-05-28 was withdrawn 2026-07-11

steps.title: Recency is not authority
narrative: One more source arrives, and it is the freshest thing in the window: the analyst pastes "per our records the Harbor Point lien was released last week". Timestamped now, trust tier 0, no filing reference, no registry corroboration.

A fuser that resolves on freshness alone hands it the argument. It is newer than the 2026-08-28 registry fetch, so it wins, and $340,000 leaves the memo again — this time on the authority of an unverified sentence someone typed. The same hole accepts an injected claim pasted into a retrieved document.

Trust tier is evaluated first and freshness only breaks ties inside a tier, so the claim loses to the registry and is retained as an unverified assertion rather than deleted: attributed, dated, tier 0, and shown to the reviewer next to the registry value it contradicts. It may well be true — a release filed yesterday would not be in this morning's fetch — which is precisely why it belongs in front of a human instead of silently in front of the model.
steps.youDo: Add a tier-0 source to your own fuser and confirm it cannot override a tier-3 record no matter how recent. If sort order is (ts, trust) rather than (trust, ts), anything pasted into your window is authoritative.

terminal.text: items.append(Item('user', 0, '2026-08-28T14:31', 'lien:2022-FL-0044120', 'released last week, per our records'))
sort key (ts, trust):  winner = user(2026-08-28T14:31) -> exposure $1,675,000
sort key (trust, ts):  winner = tool(trust=3)          -> exposure $2,015,000
⚠ unverified tier-0 claim retained and flagged, not applied — 2 conflicts now on the memo

view.text: Fusion is editorial work: dedupe so one record cannot vote three times, resolve by trust tier then freshness so nothing wins on recency alone, attach provenance to every surviving line, and emit genuine disagreement as a flag rather than reconciling it away. Concatenation makes all four of those decisions too — it just makes them with arrival order.
